title: Elders' homes
tomorrow: kiran's little brother is failing math. can teaching be seva?

lines: WHAT DO I EVEN TALK ABOUT?
cards: Bebe's oldest friend, Mohinder, lives in a care home now. Bebe usually visits on Sundays. This Sunday her knee is bad, so she hands Simran a container of saag and a slip of paper with a room number.
Simran texts Maya from the parking lot: what if she doesn't know who I am? What do I even talk about with her?

teach.b: Mohinder knows exactly who she is. Jaswant's girl, she says. The one who laughs like a truck horn.
Then the conversation stalls, and Simran remembers the Japji.

teach.h: SING, LISTEN, KEEP LOVE IN MIND.
teach.b: In its fifth pauri, Guru Nanak gives a line of plain verbs: sing, and listen, and keep love in your mind. So she asks Mohinder what Bebe was like at sixteen. And Mohinder talks.

teach.h: A VILLAGE, A WELL, A GOAT.
teach.b: A village, a well, two girls in trouble over something involving a goat. Simran listens.
Then, a little shy, she starts a shabad Bebe sings at home, and Mohinder joins in, eyes closed, every word, and a woman at the next table hums along. Here's what this week keeps building toward.
Seva isn't only food or water.
Loneliness is a hunger too, and company is a kind of langar. In a care home, a story can wait a long time for someone to ask for it.
The thing to tell a friend tonight: an hour of company is a gift no one can buy. As Simran leaves, Mohinder grips her hand. Next Sunday, she says, tell Jaswant the goat story is hers to finish.

how: Sikh youth and sangat groups visit elders at home and in care homes as seva, bringing food, listening and singing shabads together.

o: hospitals that care only for very sick elders
group homes a gurdwara runs for its own members
care homes where seva is mainly keeping company

games.q: company for the old — tap the pairs.
p: sing, listen, keep love in mind

s: seva at a care home means doing tasks for the staff
the seva is company: singing, listening, keeping love in mind.
the Japji's fifth pauri says sing, and listen, and keep love in your mind
a line of plain verbs for any visit.

games.q: your grandpa tells the same fishing story every single visit. you've heard it ten times. what does the Japji's line suggest?
o: listen again, and ask one new question about it.
gently remind him he's told it, so you can move on.
visit less often, so the story will feel fresh.
games.why: sing, and listen, and keep love in your mind. a story heard again with one new question is company; the story was never really the point.

practice: Say out loud the name of one elder you know or knew: a grandparent, a neighbor, a teacher. Then say one thing they taught you, even something small, in their words if you remember them. Let their name stay with you through the sit.

wordCard.voice: Elders' homes. Care homes where older people live; the seva there is company. Bhaao is love, kept in mind.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: bhaao, love; from the Japji's sing, and listen, and keep love in your mind.

carryVoice: Your line: company for the old. An hour is a gift nobody can buy. Bye for now.

sources.ref: Japji, pauri 5 (Ang 2: gaaveeai suneeai man rakheeai bhaao), paraphrased
